chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Abdullah ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Abdullah, the slave of Abd Rabbih, wholed of Abd Rabbih, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the gemstone which is extracted from the mine, and in it are gold, silver, and brass all together, how do we buy it? So he (peace be upon him) said: You buy it with the gold and the silver entirely.
ai.seo_question: How to buy mixed gold, silver, and brass from a mine according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the mechanism of *sarf* (currency exchange) for mixed ores containing gold, silver, and brass (*sufr*). The ruling establishes that the transaction is valued and executed based on the precious metals (gold and silver), effectively treating the brass as part of the bulk or excluding it from the primary currency calculation, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of prioritizing intrinsic value in mixed commodities.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Abdullah Bin Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Abdullah, a slave of Abd Rabbih who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the gems which are extracted from the mines and therein is gold, and silver, and brass altogether, how to buy it?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘You should buy it with the gold and the silver entirely’.
en.sarwar: 22. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-FIusayn ibn Sa‘id from ‘Abd Allah ibn Yahya from ibn Muskan from abu ‘Abd Allah, Mawla “Abd Rabbihi who has said the following:

“This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a substance that was taken from the mine in which there were gold, silver and zinc. How could we buy it? He (the Imam) said, ‘You can buy it with both gold and silver.’”
